'''Decipher and the ''Star Wars'' CCG Lucasfilm license''' covers [[Decipher]]'s license to publish the ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game, its pitch to keep it, and the license's end on 31 December 2001, after which Lucasfilm gave the card-game rights to Wizards of the Coast and Decipher handed SWCCG to the volunteer [[Players Committee]].

== The license ==

Decipher was meeting Lucasfilm at Skywalker Ranch as a licensee by November 1994, while developing its ''Star Wars'' game.<ref name="vapilot1994" /> [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] shipped in December 1995. In 1998 Lucasfilm renewed the license and extended it to ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="duelist25" />

== The pitch to keep the license ==

[[File:Skywalker-Ranch-presentation-card-encyc.png|thumb|right|300px|The Skywalker Ranch card Decipher showed Lucasfilm.<ref name="encyc3" />]]

In July 2000 Decipher pitched Lucasfilm executives on its plans for the license.<ref name="pres2000" /> It proposed marketing programs (sweepstakes for walk-on roles, set visits and Ranch visits, World Championship prizes, George Lucas signature cards, in-theater promotions, mall tours and fast-food premiums), a digital ''Star Wars'' CCG, and a backward-compatible SWCCG 2nd Edition for 2001. It asked Lucasfilm to treat card games as a core category, give earlier access to film material, ease channel restrictions and avoid over-licensing, and it pointed to roughly a quarter of a billion dollars that customers had spent on Decipher's ''Star Wars'' games. Lucasfilm approved none of it.<ref name="pres2000" />

As part of the pitch, Decipher showed Lucasfilm a mock-up Location card, '''•Skywalker Ranch''': "If you occupy, Decipher gets the CCG license here."<ref name="encyc3" />

After the loss, Chairman [[Warren Holland]] said Decipher had offered Lucasfilm more money than for any previous license, and blamed the influence of Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast and a push toward younger, ''Pokémon''-style games. He did not disclose the terms of a settlement with Lucasfilm.<ref name="icv2-2002" /><ref name="tfn2001" />

== End of the license ==

Decipher announced on 28 December 2001 that Lucasfilm would not extend the license.<ref name="ann122801" /><ref name="tfn2001" /> Wizards of the Coast received an exclusive multi-year worldwide trading-card license and planned a new game with ''Episode II'' content for 2002.<ref name="icv2-2002" /> Decipher could no longer make SWCCG expansions, and cards in development were never released.<ref name="wp-swccg" /> See [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]].

== Handoff to the Players Committee ==

In January 2002 Decipher created the volunteer Players Committee to run tournaments, rulings and support for the game.<ref name="pc1" /> The Committee may issue new cards only electronically and for free, with no new film images; see [[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement]] and [[History of the Players Committee]].<ref name="pcabout" />
